Inhomogeneity is reduced from 24.1% to 17.5% in simulation with realistic human body models, and from 18.5% to 13.9% in phantom measurements. Furthermore, the SAR efficiency is improved by 26% in simulation. In receive, the measured SNR is improved by a factor of 1.48 at the center, compared to a 1.76 improvement with equivalent channel count conventional surface coil array. CONCLUSION: The proposed combination of MS and MM operating dually as a passive field lens and receive array improves homogeneity, SAR efficiency, and receive sensitivity for 3 T abdominal MRI.

articles.title: Long-term trends and projections of CT and MRI utilization across selected OECD countries: a framework for sustainable imaging service planning.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: CT and MRI utilization is increasing across high-income countries, partly because of population ageing. This study integrated cross-country trends in examination rates, demographic change, and scanner productivity across OECD countries to project utilization to 2050 and inform sustainable service planning. MATERIALS AND METHODS: CT and MRI examination rates were obtained from the OECD Data Explorer and Japan's National Database of Health Insurance Claims Open Data. Population data were derived from the United Nations World Population Prospects 2024. Linear regression projected examination rates to 2050. Pearson coefficients assessed associations between imaging rates and population shares aged 0-14, 15-64, and ≥ 65 years. Scanner productivity was calculated as annual examinations per device. RESULTS: CT utilization was strongly associated with the population aged ≥ 65 years in all countries (r = 0.95-1.00). MRI showed similarly strong associations in most countries (r = 0.95-0.99), with Italy as the main exception. Linear extrapolation projected CT rates of approximately 722 examinations per 1000 population in Korea and 520 in the United States by 2050, while MRI rates reached approximately 327 in France and 308 in Germany. Population-level utilization did not consistently correspond to device-level productivity; CT examinations per scanner ranged from 2153.3 in Japan to 11,526.5 in Canada. CONCLUSIONS: Population ageing was associated with increasing CT and MRI utilization. Future demand may also depend on health system organization and scanner productivity. Sustainable planning should integrate demographic forecasting, appropriateness stewardship, operational optimization, workforce development, and technological innovation rather than rely solely on proportional capacity expansion. KEY POINTS: Question Ageing drives CT/MRI demand (r = 0.95-1.00 for CT); projected to continue to 2050, offering a valuable planning window. Findings High utilization ≠ high scanner productivity; operational organization shapes imaging output independently of demand volume. Critical relevance statement Sustainable planning requires demographic forecasting, appropriateness management, and technological innovation, not just capacity expansion.

articles.title: A Fully Automated Segment-Specific CCTA Plaque Quantification Workflow using Deep Learning.
articles.abstract: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) remains essential for diagnosing coronary artery disease, while the focus has moved from stenosis to plaque burden. Current workflows either need manual adjustments that limit consistency and efficiency, or they lack segment-specific precision. This study evaluated the effectiveness and reliability of a fully automated deep learning-based plaque quantification method using CCTA. DVPlaque workflow, a fully automated deep learning model, was developed to quantify segment-specific plaque volume. A total of 271 CCTA scans were included. Plaque quantification was performed by the expert and DVPlaque model, respectively. Reliability was measured through interclass correlation coefficient (ICC) analysis and Bland-Altman plots. DVPlaque workflow cost less time than expert measurement (p < 0.0001). Among these segments of major coronary arteries, proximal left ascending artery (LAD) had the highest prevalence of plaque (97.0%). Among these coronary arteries, the volumes of total plaque (TP), calcified plaque (CP), noncalcified plaque (NCP), and low-density NCP were the highest in LAD (all p-values < 0.05). On a per-patient level, the ICCs for TP, CP, and NCP volume were 0.962, 0.985, and 0.932. The corresponding biases and 95% limits of agreement were - 25.39 [ - 261.51, 210.73] mm3, 11.88 [ - 52.78, 76.55] mm3, and - 37.27 [ - 255.88, 181.33] mm3. For TP, CP, and NCP, per-vessel ICCs were all > 0.90, and per-segment ICCs were > 0.90 except for mid-LAD NCP (0.887). DVPlaque scheme was capable of quantifying plaque volume with excellent efficiency. The automated quantification of CP and NCP exhibited strong reliability even on a per-segment level, facilitating clinical application.

articles.title: Nondisease Sources of Radiomic Texture Variation on Plain Radiographs: A Cross-Sectional Analysis of Anatomical Region, Projection, and Resolution in a Public Fracture Archive.
articles.abstract: Radiomic texture features from plain radiographs feed machine learning models on the assumption that they reflect tissue rather than anatomy or acquisition. In a public multihospital fracture archive, we quantified how anatomical region and radiographic projection, each adjusted for the other and for image resolution, shift 17 radiomic features, how much feature variance resolution explains, and a bony superimposition contrast defined within region. This retrospective cross-sectional secondary analysis used FracAtlas (4083 musculoskeletal radiographs from three hospitals); 4024 images were analyzed. For each z-scored feature (10 first-order, 7 Gy-level co-occurrence matrix [GLCM]), linear models estimated adjusted differences (β, SD units), and resolution by variance explained (R2), with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction within each factor. Superimposition (hip and shoulder vs hand and leg; n = 3630), a grouping of regions, was analyzed as a pooled regional contrast rather than an independent factor. Region shifted 16 of 17 features (radiomic uniformity, hand vs leg - 0.66 SD [95% CI - 0.72 to - 0.59]). Resolution explained up to 16.8% of single-feature variance and changed the fracture log-odds coefficient by more than 15% for 7 of 10 interpretable features. Projection had the smallest effects (radiomic 10th percentile, lateral vs frontal - 0.32 SD). The superimposition contrast produced the largest shifts (GLCM energy - 2.26 SD [95% CI - 2.36 to - 2.16]). Radiomic texture on plain radiographs varies substantially with anatomy and acquisition, independently of fracture status. Radiograph radiomics studies should record and adjust for region, projection, and resolution, report region-specific estimates, and validate across sites.

articles.title: AI-Based Low-Dose Chest CT Assessment of Coronary Artery Calcification Score: An Analysis of Accuracy-Relating Factors.
articles.abstract: This study evaluates the accuracy of AI-based coronary artery calcium scoring on nongated low-dose chest CT and identifies factors affecting calcium risk classification, using ECG-gated noncontrast cardiac CT as the reference standard. This prospective study included 312 patients with chest pain who underwent ECG-gated noncontrast cardiac CT and additional low-dose chest CT (LDCT). LDCT images were reconstructed using pulmonary and standard kernels. AI software automatically quantified Agatston, mass, volume, and total coronary artery calcium scores (CACSs). Patients were stratified by Agatston-based risk category, heart rate (≤ 65 vs. > 65 bpm), and BMI (< 25 vs. ≥ 25 kg/m2). Agreement, systematic bias, and risk classification performance were assessed using Bland-Altman analysis, ICC analysis, Friedman tests with Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons, linear regression, and confusion matrices. Pulmonary kernel LDCT produced Agatston scores comparable to ECG-gated CT, with no significant differences across heart rate, BMI, or calcium severity subgroups. Under this kernel, measurement bias showed weak but significant correlations with heart rate and BMI (r = 0.145 and r = 0.131, respectively; both P < 0.05). Overall, nongated LDCT-derived CACS correlated strongly with reference CACS (r > 0.94). The low heart rate/low-BMI subgroup showed the best risk stratification performance, with 80% accuracy and good agreement (κ = 0.72). AI-assisted CACS assessment on nongated low-dose chest CT may serve as an adjunctive tool for opportunistic coronary artery calcification screening and preliminary cardiovascular risk stratification. Its accuracy may be influenced by reconstruction kernel and calcification burden, whereas heart rate and BMI may not be significant influencing factors.Trial Registration: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2500100073,2 April 2025, the study was retrospectively registered).

articles.title: Cross-Center Stroke Evaluation using Carotid Ultrasound Patterns via Scale-Adaptive Frequency-Enhanced Neural Network.
articles.abstract: Medical imaging datasets vary across institutions due to differences in scanner types, posing challenges for model generalization. To address the issue, this study proposed a scale-adaptive frequency-enhanced neural network (SAFE-Net), which leveraged a DWT-ViT encoder to incorporate frequency-domain features into a transformer-based architecture for cross-center stroke evaluation. The discrete wavelet transform (DWT) decomposed carotid color Doppler (CCD) images into multiresolution frequency sub-bands. The extracted high-resolution (Xh) and low-resolution (Xl) features are concatenated to enhance both local and global feature extraction. Experimental results demonstrated that SAFE-Net achieves the highest accuracy, with 92.5% accuracy on Institution A and 93.75% on Institution B, outperforming other models in stroke evaluation. SAFE-Net maintains cross-center generalization, with an accuracy of 90.73% when trained on Institution A and tested on Institution B, and 89.16% in the reverse setting. Also, the model required 25% fewer parameters and 2.0× fewer FLOPs than conventional models. These findings underscored the effectiveness of SAFE-Net across diverse medical imaging datasets.

articles.title: ParetoRx: A Multiobjective Radiogenomic Framework Integrating Pareto Optimization and Q-Learning for Exploratory Compound Prioritization in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
articles.abstract: Imaging-defined high-risk phenotypes may capture biologically aggressive disease states, but translating them into therapeutic hypotheses remains challenging. We developed ParetoRx, a radiogenomic imaging-informatics framework integrating computed tomography radiomics, pathway-level transcriptomic analysis, multiobjective Pareto optimization, and model-free Q-learning for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Pretreatment CT data from 402 patients were used for model development and internal validation, with 110 patients forming a held-out external cohort. The final radiomics model achieved an external C-index of 0.707 (95% CI 0.627-0.783); high-risk patients had worse overall survival (HR 3.461, 95% CI 1.674-7.153), with minimal change after adjustment for histology (HR 3.444, 95% CI 1.662-7.137). Gene set enrichment and single-sample pathway analyses identified exploratory associations involving E2F targets, MYC targets V1, inflammatory response, and hypoxia, although no pathway met FDR < 0.05. LINCS L1000 perturbational profiles were evaluated using transcriptomic reversal, pathway specificity, and a feasibility-related proxy, with 4188 compounds retained in the common complete-case analysis. Multiobjective Pareto optimization was combined with three-split consensus ranking and sequential policy evaluation. TWS-119 showed consistent prioritization across all three splits (ranks 1, 3, and 4) and was Pareto-optimal in each split. In simulation-based evaluation, model-free Q-learning achieved higher terminal-goal attainment than myopic and static policies across all three splits, with improvements of approximately 6.2-13.3 percentage points over the myopic comparator. These findings support ParetoRx as an exploratory framework for biologically informed compound prioritization and computational sequential decision-making, while independent drug response and clinical validation remain necessary.

articles.title: Panognostics-Plus: An Integrated Multi-Task AI Framework for Automated Panoramic Radiograph Interpretation with Dental Charting and Structured Reporting-Development and Technical Validation Study.
articles.abstract: Dental charting from panoramic radiographs is essential for clinical assessment, yet remains time-consuming. This study presents Panognostics-Plus, an automated cloud-based AI framework for panoramic radiograph analysis integrating dental charting and structured radiological reporting. Panognostics-Plus was developed using a retrospective dataset of 1,595 panoramic radiographs and a YOLO-based architecture comprising modules for dental anatomy, dental treatment, and periapical diagnostics. Anatomical structures and dental treatments were analyzed using a two-stage pipeline, whereas periapical lesions were analyzed by detection-and-classification. YOLOv8m, YOLOv9m, YOLO11m, and YOLO26m were benchmarked. Detection was evaluated by precision, sensitivity, F1-score, AP, and mAP; segmentation by IoU and Dice; and processing time. Model differences were assessed using Friedman tests with Holm-adjusted Wilcoxon signed-rank post-hoc comparisons. YOLO26m achieved the highest overall performance. The largest mAP0@50:0.95 gains were observed for crowns (+ 21.3%), radicular cysts (+ 20.5%), root canal treatments (+ 17.3%), bridges (+ 14.3%), periodontal bone level (+ 14.3%), and periapical granulomas (+ 13.5%). Dental implants achieved precision, sensitivity, and F1-score of 0.99, 0.98, and 0.98, respectively. Radicular cysts achieved precision, sensitivity, and F1-score of 0.95, 0.93, and 0.94 versus 0.92, 0.90, and 0.91 for periapical granulomas. Significant differences were observed in 8 of 10 detection tasks and all segmentation tasks (all p < 0.001); periodontal bone level (p = 0.193) and dental fillings (p = 0.073) were nonsignificant. Dice coefficients reached 0.97 for dental anatomy and 0.96 for dental treatments. The workflow generated a segmentation overlay, dental chart, and structured radiological report in 15 ± 1.4 s per radiograph. Panognostics-Plus may improve panoramic radiograph analysis and clinical efficiency, although further validation is required.

articles.title: MDF-Net: A Decoupled Multimodal Fusion Network with Contrastive Learning for Reliable Brain Tumor Segmentation on Multi-sequence MRI.
articles.abstract: Accurate segmentation of brain tumors from multimodal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is critical for clinical diagnosis, treatment planning, and longitudinal disease monitoring. Multimodal MRI provides complementary information across sequences, yet this complementarity is entangled with substantial cross-modal redundancy. Prevailing coupled fusion schemes merge modalities into a single shared space, where discriminative tumor-specific cues and redundant shared content are blended indiscriminately, an effect further aggravated by cross-scale feature inconsistency and by the difficulty of delineating small enhancing lesions. To address these issues, we recast multimodal segmentation as a decoupled representation learning problem and propose a Multimodal Decoupled Fusion Network (MDF-Net) that explicitly disentangles the fused representation into complementary and non-redundant components. At its core, a Tri-Branch Decoupling (TBD) module separates the fused features into spatial, channel, and instance components, and a Feature Contrastive Learning (FCL) objective enforces their complementarity while suppressing inter-branch redundancy. To provide scale-aware and locally coherent features for decoupling, an Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (ASPP) module and a Local Window Self-Attention (LWSA) module jointly model multi-scale context and local dependencies, while a dedicated Small Lesion Refinement (SLR) module improves the delineation of small and ambiguous enhancing tumors through multi-scale detection and boundary-aware refinement. Extensive experiments on two publicly available benchmarks, BraTS 2023 and FeTS 2022, demonstrate that MDF-Net achieves competitive and well-balanced performance relative to recent state-of-the-art methods across tumor sub-regions and multiple evaluation metrics, with particularly accurate whole-tumor boundary delineation. Ablation studies and feature-space visualizations further confirm that explicit decoupling yields a more structured embedding space and that each component makes a complementary contribution to segmentation performance.

articles.title: Clinical Context-Dependent Value of bpMRI-Derived Imaging Representations for Prostate Cancer Risk Stratification.
articles.abstract: The objective was to evaluate the clinical context-dependent value of biparametric MRI (bpMRI)-derived imaging representations for prostate cancer (PCa) risk stratification, with emphasis on whether imaging features provide complementary information in patients within the prostate-specific antigen (PSA) gray zone. This dual-campus retrospective study included 536 patients with pathologically confirmed PCa who underwent pretreatment bpMRI. Patients were classified as low/intermediate and high-risk according to NCCN criteria. Patients from Campus 1 were randomly divided into training and internal test cohorts, and Campus 2 served as an independent test cohort. Radiomics, vision transformer, and contrastive language-image pretraining (CLIP) features were extracted from T2-weighted imaging, diffusion-weighted imaging, and apparent diffusion coefficient maps. Clinical and combined clinical-imaging models were developed. Performance was assessed using ROC analysis, calibration, decision curve analysis, and SHAP interpretation, with predefined evaluation in the PSA gray zone. In the independent test cohort, the combined model achieved the highest overall discrimination, with an AUC of 0.921, followed closely by the clinical baseline model (AUC, 0.907). Among imaging-only models, the radiomics model showed the highest overall AUC (0.844). SHAP identified PSA as the dominant predictor, indicating clinically driven overall performance. In the PSA gray zone, clinical and combined model performance declined (AUCs, 0.381 and 0.600), whereas CLIP achieved the highest AUC (0.785) and favorable net benefit. The value of bpMRI-derived imaging representations for PCa risk stratification is context-dependent. CLIP-derived representations may provide complementary discrimination when PSA-based information is less informative, supporting context-aware evaluation of imaging AI models.

articles.title: Analysis unit influences observed ACR TI-RADS risk of malignancy in operative thyroid cohorts.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Operative validations of ACR TI-RADS frequently report category-specific risks of malignancy (ROM) that exceed ACR-published estimates, commonly attributed to surgical selection bias. The effects of analysis-unit choice (patient-level versus nodule-level) and multinodular disease on these observed ROM estimates remain incompletely understood. METHODS: We analyzed 3439 thyroidectomy patients (2012-2025) with preoperative ultrasound and definitive pathology. Nodules were retrospectively re-scored according to ACR TI-RADS 2017 from structured fields and report text. Risk of malignancy was evaluated using three analysis units: patient-level maximum TI-RADS, full-cohort nodule-level, and single-nodule cohorts. Multivariable logistic regression assessed the association between multinodularity and malignancy, with sensitivity analyses evaluating lesion-matching confidence and exclusion of incidental microPTC. RESULTS: Patient-level ROM exceeded ACR-published values at TR1-TR4 (TR4 47.7%; TR5 64.9%; AUC 0.655). Full-cohort nodule-level ROM was lower at higher categories (TR4 25.3%; TR5 25.2%; AUC 0.651), whereas the single-nodule cohort restored the expected TR4-TR5 gradient (TR4 42.7%; TR5 52.4%; AUC 0.699). Among single-nodule patients, 17.8% were malignant despite a benign scored nodule. Multinodularity was not independently associated with higher malignancy odds (adjusted OR 0.60, 95% CI 0.51-0.72). CONCLUSIONS: In operative thyroid cohorts, observed ACR TI-RADS risk of malignancy estimates depend on analysis unit and lesion-attribution method. Multinodularity was not independently associated with malignancy. Future TI-RADS validations should explicitly report the analysis unit and attribution approach used.

articles.title: Structured feature disentanglement for high-fidelity unified brain MRI synthesis.
articles.abstract: Multisequence Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) provides a more reliable diagnosis in clinical applications through complementary information across sequences. However, in practice, the absence of certain MR sequences is a common problem that can lead to inconsistent analysis results. In this work, we propose a novel unified framework for synthesizing multisequence MR images, called hybrid-fusion GAN (HF-GAN). The fundamental mechanism of this work is structured feature disentanglement, which aligns the design of the architecture with the complexity of the features. A powerful many-to-one stream is constructed for the extraction of complex complementary features, while utilizing parallel, one-to-one streams to process modality-specific information. A channel attention-based fusion module (CAFF) dynamically integrates these disentangled features as a universal anatomical map into a common latent space. Then, a modality infuser transforms the features to generate the target sequence. We validated our framework on public datasets of both healthy and pathological brain MRI. Quantitative and qualitative results show that HF-GAN achieves state-of-the-art performance, with our 2D slice-based framework notably yielding highly competitive and efficient results compared to a leading 3D volumetric model. Furthermore, the utilization of HF-GAN for data imputation substantially improves the performance of the downstream brain tumor segmentation task, demonstrating its clinical relevance. Our source code is available on https://github.com/SSTDV-Project/HF-GAN.

articles.title: Thoracic ultrasound for assessing chest wall invasion in lung cancer with suspected chest wall involvement: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: AIM: This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of thoracic ultrasound for detecting chest wall invasion in patients with lung cancer and suspected chest wall involvement, using surgical and/or histopathologic findings as the reference standard. MATERIALS AND METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception through June 2026 for studies of thoracic ultrasound in patients with suspected chest wall invasion by lung cancer. Sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV) were pooled separately using random-intercept logistic models. Heterogeneity was quantified with I2, and leave-one-out analyses assessed robustness. The review followed PRISMA-DTA and was prospectively registered in PROSPERO. RESULTS: Four studies comprising 249 enrolled patients were included; 246 patients contributed to diagnostic accuracy analyses. Pooled sensitivity was 89.8% (95% CI, 62.4%-97.9%; I2 = 32.5%), and pooled specificity was 94.0% (95% CI, 84.1%-97.9%; I2 = 63.9%). Pooled PPV and NPV were 85.5% (95% CI, 74.4%-92.3%; I2 = 35.9%) and 96.3% (95% CI, 82.4%-99.3%; I2 = 17.0%), respectively. Leave-one-out analyses did not materially alter the findings. CONCLUSION: Thoracic ultrasound showed favourable pooled diagnostic performance for detecting chest wall invasion in selected patients with lung cancer and may complement preoperative imaging, particularly by increasing confidence in the absence of invasion. The limited evidence base, variability in diagnostic criteria and operator experience, and heterogeneity in specificity warrant cautious interpretation and validation in larger prospective studies using standardised protocols.

articles.title: RapidAI compared to RapidAI-assisted neuroradiologist interpretation in evaluating acute ischaemic stroke: A local experience.
articles.abstract: AIM: Despite RapidAI's widescale adoption for acute stroke management, gaps remain in validating its real-world diagnostic impact. Given local observations of RapidAI overestimating infarct size for equivalent images, we evaluated the reliability of RapidAI versus neuroradiologists at a Canadian comprehensive stroke centre. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Computed tomography (CT) head and carotid studies (Jan 2020-Aug 2021) from acute stroke activations were retrospectively reviewed. Repeat presentations, no follow-up imaging within 10 days, bilateral infarcts, non-middle cerebral artery (MCA) strokes, or haemorrhage were excluded. Alberta Stroke Program Early Computed Tomography Scores (ASPECTS) from RapidAI and neuroradiologists were compared to follow-up magnetic resonance (MR) or CT imaging using intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). A linear mixed-effect model was adjusted for age and sex. Subgroup analyses examined infarct burden and infarct location (cortical vs deep). RESULTS: In total, 481 patients (49% female; median age: 74 years) were included. Neuroradiologists had higher agreement with the reference standard than RapidAI (ICC: 0.627 vs 0.546). RapidAI had a smaller adjusted difference (β = -0.10; P = 0.198) than neuroradiologists (β = 0.74; P < .001). Although agreement was poor across both groups, RapidAI showed higher agreement in extensive ischaemia (ASPECTS: 0-4: 0.194 vs 0.115; ASPECTS: 0-2: 0.083 vs 0.059), whereas neuroradiologists had higher agreement in threshold, ASPECTS: 5-7 cases (0.141 vs 0.068). Neuroradiologists showed superior agreement in deep infarcts (ICC: 0.612 vs 0.452). CONCLUSION: Neuroradiologists maintain higher overall agreement in mid-range ASPECTS cases and deep infarcts, but RapidAI exhibited higher agreement in lower ASPECTS cases. RapidAI demonstrates context-dependent accuracy, serving as an adjunct requiring cautious use alongside neuroradiologist interpretation for clinical judgement.

articles.title: High-power radiofrequency ablation with optimized pulsing algorithm for renal tumors: initial clinical experience and safety profile.
articles.abstract: Incidental diagnosis of renal cell carcinoma is increasing. While surgery remains the standard treatment for localized T1b or larger lesions, image-guided percutaneous ablation represents a valid alternative for T1a cases. Radiofrequency ablation (RFA) is effective but limited by smaller ablation volumes and sensitivity to the heat-sink effect. Microwave ablation and cryoablation have emerged to address these limitations, although the first is susceptible to thermal injury to adjacent structures and the second requires multiple, larger probes and longer procedures. High-power RFA (HP-RFA) is a recent development that delivers higher energy (370 versus 200 W), enabling faster and larger ablations. This study evaluated the feasibility and safety of a novel HP-RFA system incorporating an impedance-controlled pulsed algorithm and internally cooled electrodes. Five patients with small renal tumors (mean diameter 2.3 cm) unsuitable for surgery underwent ultrasound- or computed tomography-guided HP-RFA. Technical success, safety, and early tumor control were assessed. All procedures were technically successful. No major complications occurred; one minor perirenal hematoma was managed conservatively. Follow-up imaging at 6 months demonstrated complete tumor ablation without local recurrence. These preliminary findings suggest that HP-RFA is feasible and safe for treating small renal tumors and may represent a promising evolution of RFA. Further studies are needed. KEY POINTS: Question Can HP-RFA provide feasible and safe minimally invasive treatment for small renal tumors while overcoming limitations of conventional RFA? Findings Technical success and efficacy of HP-RFA were achieved in 100% of cases. No major complications. Complete tumor ablation was accomplished. Relevance statement HP-RFA demonstrates feasibility, safety, and effective early tumor control in small renal tumors. By enabling larger, faster ablations, it may overcome limitations of conventional RFA and expand the employment of minimally invasive treatment options instead of surgical approaches.

articles.title: MRI-based virtual radiographs of the pelvis for assessment of acetabular morphology.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: We generated magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based virtual radiographs (VRs) from hips with/without intra-articular contrast and compared them with conventional anteroposterior pelvic radiographs (CR) regarding measurement bias, interobserver and intraobserver agreement, and diagnosis of acetabular deformities; we also assessed hip deformity prevalence on VR in asymptomatic participants. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Retrospective study of 50 patients (100 hips; mean age 34 years) with femoroacetabular impingement or hip dysplasia undergoing CR and unilateral magnetic resonance arthrography. Additionally, 53 asymptomatic participants underwent noncontrast MRI. Segmentation of the osseous pelvis was performed on T1-weighted volume interpolated breathhold examination (VIBE) Dixon MRI using 3D nnU-Net, pseudo-computed tomography generation, and cone-beam projection to generate VR. Acetabular coverage (lateral center edge angle (LCE), acetabular index (AI), anterior/posterior coverage, extrusion index (EI)), and acetabular version were compared between CR and VR. Interobserver agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) and κ statistics; bias with Bland-Altman analysis. RESULTS: Interobserver agreement for VR ranged from moderate to almost perfect (ICC/κ 0.60-0.94), except for the AI. LCE showed no significant bias with ( - 0.2° ± 2.5, p = 0.663) or without contrast ( - 0.2° ± 2.2, p = 0.530). Systematic differences occurred for AI, EI, anterior/posterior coverage, and ischial spine sign; 57-75% of discrepancies were within CR interobserver variation. Diagnostic classification showed substantial agreement between CR and VR (κ = 0.62), comparable to CR interobserver agreement (κ = 0.70). In asymptomatic participants, 13% had acetabular dysplasia, 68% normal coverage, and 19% overcoverage. CONCLUSION: MRI-based VR provides acetabular morphology assessment comparable to CR and enables radiation-free evaluation in symptomatic patients and asymptomatic populations. KEY POINTS: Question Can MRI-based virtual radiographs reproduce conventional radiographic measurements of acetabular morphology, enabling radiation-free two-dimensional assessment in symptomatic patients and asymptomatic populations? Findings The lateral center-edge angle showed no significant bias between virtual and conventional radiographs; diagnostic classification of acetabular deformities agreed substantially (κ = 0.62), comparable to conventional radiograph interobserver agreement. Relevance Statement MRI-derived virtual radiographs can provide acetabular measurements comparable to conventional radiographs without ionizing radiation, supporting integration into three-dimensional surgical planning and enabling assessment in young patients and population-based cohorts where repeated radiographs are undesirable.

articles.title: Oxygen-enhanced brain MRI using dynamic gradient-echo and MR fingerprinting.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Oxygen-enhanced brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) using dynamic three-dimensional (3D) gradient-echo and MR fingerprinting (MRF) was applied to evaluate oxygen transit from blood to cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). MATERIALS AND METHODS: Twenty healthy participants, enrolled between December 2023 and March 2024, underwent 3-T MRI including Pre-oxygen inhalation 3D MRF (pre-O₂ MRF), dynamic 3D gradient-echo (volumetric interpolated breath-hold examination, VIBE) during oxygen inhalation, and post-oxygen inhalation 3D MRF (post-O₂ MRF). Pre-O₂ and post-O₂ MRF each consisted of two acquisitions. Signal intensity on dynamic VIBE and T1 relaxation times from MRF were evaluated in gray matter (GM), white matter (WM), surface CSF, and ventricles using volumes of interest (VOIs). RESULTS: Dynamic 3D VIBE demonstrated a rapid signal increase in surface CSF immediately after oxygen inhalation, with a smaller increase in GM. Post-oxygen inhalation VIBE signal was significantly higher than pre-oxygen inhalation signal in surface CSF (p < 0.001) and GM (p < 0.001). T1 relaxation times differed significantly across phases for GM, WM, and surface CSF (p < 0.001) as well as for ventricles (p = 0.024). Large effect sizes were observed for surface CSF (Cohen dz = 4.15) and GM (Cohen dz = 1.31) in dynamic 3D VIBE, as well as for surface CSF (Cohen f = 1.31) and GM (Cohen f = 0.73) in T1 relaxation time measurement, suggesting substantial physiological changes following oxygen inhalation. CONCLUSION: Dynamic 3D VIBE images visualized oxygen inhalation-related signal change in the surface CSF, which were quantitatively validated by T1 relaxation time reductions derived from 3D MRF. KEY POINTS: Question Can noninvasive oxygen-enhanced brain MRI visualize and quantify oxygen-related signal changes in cerebrospinal fluid using dynamic 3D gradient-echo and 3D MR fingerprinting? Findings Dynamic 3D gradient-echo showed rapid surface CSF signal increases after oxygen inhalation, accompanied by significant T1 reductions on 3D MR fingerprinting. Relevance statement This noninvasive oxygen-enhanced MR approach may provide a clinically feasible method for assessing oxygen transit into CSF and could support future investigations of human CSF dynamics. Dynamic 3D gradient-echo images visualized oxygen inhalation-related signal change in the surface CSF, which were quantitatively validated by T1 relaxation time reductions derived from 3D MRF.

articles.title: Combining shear wave elastography and ultrasound localization microscopy for liver fibrosis staging in a rat model.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Accurate staging of liver fibrosis (LF) remains a clinical challenge. This study aimed to quantitatively evaluate the diagnostic value of combining shear wave elastography (SWE) and ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM) for LF staging across the full disease spectrum. We sought to integrate liver mechanical properties and microvascular structural parameters to build a multiparametric model for fibrosis staging. MATERIALS AND METHODS: LF was induced in Sprague-Dawley rats and histologically staged according to the METAVIR system. A total of 62 rats were included in the final analysis. Both SWE and ULM were performed in each animal. Liver viscoelastic moduli were estimated from SWE data using SW-VEI-Net, a physics-informed neural network-based approach. ULM data were post-processed to reconstruct super-resolution images of the hepatic microvasculature, followed by quantitative analysis to extract microvascular structural parameters. RESULTS: Histology revealed fibrosis stages F0 (n = 10), F1 (n = 12), F2 (n = 19), F3 (n = 11), and F4 (n = 10). Compared with the single-modality SWE and ULM models, the multiparametric combined model achieved the highest numerical areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve across the four classification tasks: 0.93 for F0 versus F1-F4, 0.92 for F0-F1 versus F2-F4, 0.90 for F0-F2 versus F3-F4, and 0.89 for F0-F3 versus F4. CONCLUSION: Combining SWE-derived viscoelastic parameters with ULM-derived microvascular features enabled multiparametric characterization of LF in this preclinical rat model. Independent validation in larger animal cohorts and, ultimately, human studies is essential before robust clinical conclusions can be drawn. KEY POINTS: Question Can combining shear-wave elastography (SWE) and ULM improve the accuracy of LF staging? Findings By integrating viscoelastic and microvascular features, the SWE-ULM combined model achieved the highest numerical AUCs across all four fibrosis classifications in a rat model. Relevance statement The SWE and ULM combined model suggests potential value for LF staging by integrating viscoelastic and microvascular biomarkers, providing a basis for further investigation toward future clinical translation.

articles.title: Magnetic resonance angiography based on iron-coordinated poly(amino acid)s nanoprobes: an in vitro and in vivo experimental study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To develop a gadolinium-free T1-weighted magnetic resonance (MR) contrast nanoprobe using Fe(III)-poly(amino acid)s-coordinated complexes (Fe@polyDOPA-b-polysarcosine, Fe@POS) for high-resolution MR angiography (MRA) with an extended imaging window. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Fe@POS nanoprobes were prepared by the self-assembly of Fe(III) and polyDOPA-b-polysarcosine copolymers. Physicochemical and cytological characterizations were conducted to demonstrate their feasibility for MRA. MRA of the aorta was conducted on New Zealand rabbits, which were divided into one experimental group (n = 3) receiving Fe@POS nanoprobes and one control group (n = 3) receiving Gadolinium diethylenetriamine pentaacetic acid (Gd-DTPA). Cardiac and hepatic MR acquisition were conducted on Bama Swine (n = 3). Long-term biodistribution (n = 3) and biosafety (n = 4) evaluation was performed on BALB/c mice. Short-term and acute toxicity evaluation was conducted on BALB/c mice (n = 5) and Bama pigs (n = 3). RESULTS: Fe@POS nanoprobes exhibited a regular nanomicelle structure with an average particle size of 25 nm. Compared with Gd-DTPA (r1 = 4.38 mM-1 s-1), Fe@POS nanoprobes exhibited higher longitudinal relaxivity (r1 = 5.74 mM-1 s-1). In rabbit models, significant MR signal enhancement was observed in the abdominal aorta for over 4 h post-injection of Fe@POS. In porcine models, prolonged T1 enhancement was observed on MRA of the cardiovascular system, revealing detailed arterial and venous vasculature system in MR images. The biosafety evaluations demonstrated that the Fe@POS nanoprobes exhibited satisfactory biocompatibility and no prolonged iron accumulation in major organs under the tested conditions. CONCLUSION: Fe@POS nanoprobes simultaneously provided high-resolution T1-weighted MRA of the cardiovascular system with an extended imaging window. KEY POINTS: Question Can a gadolinium-free nanoprobe provide prolonged high-resolution T1-weighted magnetic resonance angiography? Findings The use of Fe (III)-based poly(amino acid)s nanoprobes enables high-spatial-resolution magnetic resonance angiography of the cardiovascular system with a long window period. CRITICAL RELEVANCE: The development of this new MRI contrast agent could broaden its clinical applicability and contribute to more precise diagnoses of cardiovascular diseases.
